         JEROME AND GAYLYNN SNEED'S REPLY TO EXCEPTIONS TO THE
                        PROPOSAL FOR DECISION

        Jerome and Gaylynn Sneed timely submitl the following Reply to Exceptions to the

Proposal for Decision ("PFD"), and would respectfully show as follows:

        The PFD correctly recommends that the Commission deny the Application. Should the

Commission nonetheless approve the Application and select a route, Route 891 is the fairest to

landowners and most reasonable to ratepayers based on a holistic analysis. Therefore, the Sneeds

reply to exceptions recommending Routes 894 or 487.2

                                    I.        REPLY TO EXCEPTIONS

        The Permian Basin Reliability Plan ("Plan")3 fails to establish need for the CCN project.

The Sneeds take exception to Staffand other parties' arguments that the PFD did not give sufficient




        1 Exceptions and Replies Memorandum at 1 Aug. 20,2026)
        2 See, e . g., CE Stephens Properties LLC Exceptions to the PFD ( Sept . 2 , 2026 ); Commission Staff' s
Exceptions to the PFD (Sept. 2,2026)
        3 See , e · g ·, Applicants ' Exceptions to the PFD ( Sept . 2 , 2026 ); Commission Staff' s Exceptions to the PFD
(Sept. 2,2026)

                                                           1
 weight to ERCOT' s recommendations in the Plan.4                        First, when approving the Plan, the

Commission made clear in its order that applicants "must establish in the CCN proceeding that the

certificate meets all applicable legal requirements for a CCN, including the requirement set forth

in PURA § 37 . 056 ( a) that the certificate is necessary for the service, accommodation ,

convenience, or safety of the public."5 The Commission issued this mandate qfter the Plan was

drafted and presented to the Commission. There was no establishment of need in this proceeding

as required by the Commission.               Instead, the j oint applicants relied on the Permian Basin

Reliability Plan itself, contrary to the Commission' s directives to prove need. Second, ERCOT

has acknowledged miscalculations in the load forecast underpinning the Plan,6 Staff has stated

"changes are needed" to the forecast,7 and the PUCT has found that the forecast is unrealistic. 8

The PFD' s finding that Applicants have failed to independently justify need is correct.

        If the application is approved, the Commission should select Route 891, which was not

included in Staff' s or many others' routing analysis-another factor supporting the lack of due

process found by the PFD. Parties supporting Routes 894 and 487 may be able to point to strengths

on individual criteria, but cannot match Route 891's overall performance across all the

Commission' s routing factors, especially bisecting fewer miles of landowner property and

lowering overall cost to ratepayers:




        4 See , e · g ·, Applicants ' Exceptions to the PFD ( Sept . 2 , 2026 ); Commission Staff' s Exceptions to the PFD
(Sept. 2,2026)
         5 project NO · 5571 %, Reliability Plan for the Permian Basin Region Under PURA § 39. 167, Final Order at 5
(Oct. 5,2024) (emphasis added).
         6 PFD at 77 ; Project No . 59772 , Proceeding to Adjust the 2026 Load Forecast Used By ERCOT, ERCOT
Proposal to Adjust Long-Tenn Load Forecast (May 18, 2026).
          7 PFD at 76; Hearing on the Merits Transcript at 287, 285-90 (Intervenor Judy Graci Cross of Commission
Staff witness John Poole) (June 9,2026)
        8 PFD at 77 (quoting from Commission Order finding that "adjusting the Long-Term Load Forecast to a
more realistic value may be warranted").

                                                           2
               •   Bisecting Landowner Properties - Route 891 bisects fewer miles of landowner
                  property than Routes 894 and 487, which is the greatest factor for determining
                  impact on landowners.9 In comparison, 894 bisects over 6 miles more landowner
                  property and 487 bisects over 10 miles more landowner property than Route 891.
              •   Cost - The estimated cost of Route 891 is $1,671,949,000-nearly $9 million less
                  expensive than Route 894.10
              •   Environmental Impact - Route 891 provides the greatest setbacks from the
                  sensitive Lampasas and San Saba Rivers.11

         For convenience, a side-by-side comparison of key metrics is provided as Attachment A.

A detailed narrative analysis of routing comparisons is provided in the Sneeds' Exceptions,

briefing to the ALJ, and expert testimony of Karen Hubbard, who testified that the proposed

trisecting12 of the Sneeds' Ranch is the most egregious she has ever seen. 13

         It is important to note that parties' Exceptions present various route comparisons, yet omit

Route 891 entirely, which seems to have influenced the PFD. That omission is telling in that

different results would have been reached had Route 891 been included in the analysis. For

example, Staffwas not able to review Ms. Hubbard' s or Mr. Sneed's analysis ofRoute 891 before

the hearingl4 due to time constraints and the volume of testimonies. Additionally, Staff"s routing

analysis did not analyze all routes. Staff only had time to review the routes highlighted in an Oncor




         9 A side-by-side comparison of key metrics is provided as Attachment A.
         10 Id.
        11 Attachment B is a map showing the relative setbacks from the Lampasas River and San Saba River among
Routes 891, 894, and 487.
         12 Attachment C is an aerial view depicting the proposed route fragmenting the Sneed Ranch into three
sections where traveling from the northeast corner to northwest corner would require crossing the line twice.
         13 Hearing on the Merits Transcript at 114:1-4 (June 11, 2026) ("I've rarely seen fragmentation bisection to
the extent of the Sneeds' property. It simply cuts it into three pieces and it's pretty egregious, and that's one of the
reasons I agreed to testify.")
        14 Hearing on the Merits Transcript at 92:6-16 (Poole Cross) (June 10, 2026) (Q: "I think you have not had
an opportunity to review [Route 891] or compare that at this time. Is that right?" A: "That's correct. Yes.")

                                                           3
 memorandum, 15 which did not include Route 891. Still, once presented with Route 891 Staff stated

that it clearly outperformed Staff's alternative recommendation on multiple key criteria. 16

         The Commission' s task is broader, however, than any single party's comparison: it must

evaluate the routes on the full record before it, rather than limiting its review to the set of routes

another party chose to analyze. A simple review of Attachment A shows that Route 891 is the

fairest to landowners, as it bisects property at least five and a half miles less than the next most

comparable route, and is $9 million less expensive than the primary route recommended in the

PFD.

         Many parties' exceptions recommend Route 296, which the Sneeds would support as being

the second least intrusive among the Routes of Interest to landowners in terms of bisecting

property.


                                 II.      CONCLUSION AND PRAYER

         For the foregoing reasons, the Sneeds respectfully request that the Commission adopt the

PFD's recommendation to deny the Application.                   In the alternative, should the Commission

approve the Application, the Sneeds request that the Commission select Routes 891 or 296.




         15 Oncor & LCRA TSC Exhibit No. 1, Application at Attachment 11, Routing Memo.
         16 Hearing on the Merits Transcript at 92:6-16, 92:21-94:11 (Poole Cross) (June 10,2026) (acknowledging
that Route 891 performs better or comparably on cost, paralleling comparable ROW, avoiding habitable structures,
and avoiding riparian areas compared to Route 296, which Staff ranks as superior to Route 894); Reply Brief of Jerome
and Gaylynn Sneed at 7 (June 26,2026)
